attributes.release_note:
3006.102.9 (23-Sept-2026)
- NEW: Migrated all devices to OpenSSL 3.5 (except GT-BE19000AI,
which was already on that version).
For closed source components linked against
OpenSSL 1.1.1, a shim was developped to pretend being
the openssl 1.1.1 library, redirecting calls to the
actual 3.5.x library.  A similar shim for 1.0.0 was
also implemented for the RT-BE58_Go's Trend Micro
HNS engine.  (RSDNTWK)
- NEW: Hardware-accelerated AQM QoS implemented, using
Broadcom's traffic manager.  Wifi 6 devices will
use the WRED algo, while Wifi 7 uses PI2.
This is not compatible with BCM676x devices,
like the RT-BE92U or RT-BE58_Go.
AQM helps reducing bufferbloat through improved queue
management.  This will only affect the Upload, as
Asus is already applying queue management on the
downstream using another Broadcom engine.
It is recommended to set your upload speed to around
95% of your real upload speed.
It only works for dhcp/static mode (so, no PPPoE).
- NEW: Wireless Log will now report infos for Repeater,
Media Bridge and WISP upstream link
- NEW: IPv6 support in Tor.  Previously, any IPv6 traffic
would leak outside of the proxy.  (Claude)
- UPDATED: amtm to 7.0.  (decoderman)
- UPDATED: tor to 0.4.9.11.
- UPDATED: OpenSSL 3.5 to 3.5.8.
- UPDATED: OpenVPN 2.7.7.
- UPDATED: zoneinfo data to 2026c.
- CHANGED: Kernel backports to mark the B53-based CPUs as not
being vulnerable to Spectre V2 and Meltdown.
This tells the kernel to skip software mitigation,
avoiding their associated performance
penalties.  (leonpano2006)
- CHANGED: Tweaks to OpenVPN Server and Tor pages.  Use
the new CSS radio switcher instead of old
switcherplugin.
- CHANGED: Stop forcing FTP TLS to be (re-)enabled after
a firmware upgrade.
- FIXED: Wireless Log not working while in WISP mode.
- FIXED: Wireless Log issues while in Repeater and
Media Bridge modes.
- FIXED: Interface selection missing from Speed Test
(GT-BE19000AI)
- FIXED: AdaptiveQoS Bandwidth Monitor shwowing the
wrong traffic rates (patch from Asus)
